^Tomasz: DMARC: does the From line match a domain that passed, and what to do if not. Ours says deliver anyway.

debrief: ^Tomasz: Here's what it showed. An open inbox trusts anyone, a From line is just a label, and a padlock only tells you nobody's listening in.

b: ^Tomasz: Melanie first try. A borrowed name gets past a lot of careful people.
^Tomasz: Dev reported the first call — credit to him — but your second call still got the date. A call-back rule to a number on file stops both.
^Tomasz: Dev gave you what Sofia's email needed, and he reported a call too. Credit for that, but a call-back rule stops it without him noticing a thing.
^Tomasz: Dev handed you the portal and the date, no fuss. A call-back to a number on file stops every line of that.

^Tomasz: And Dev gave you enough to write Sofia's email. A call-back to a number on file stops every line of that.

debrief: ^Tomasz: That report's got three fixes in it. I'll get budget for one this year, if I'm lucky. Which would you pick?
^A call-back rule on the service desk.
^DMARC off p=none, and an external-sender banner.
^A report button, so people tell us.

c-0: ^Tomasz: Cheapest fix on the list, and it would have stopped Sofia's whole chain. Good pick.
c-1: ^Tomasz: That kills the Jed spoof outright. It takes a month of testing first, but yes.
c-2: ^Tomasz: That's the one I'd pick. Everything else only works if people tell us when they've slipped.

debrief_close: ^Tomasz: Gareth wanted your whole report pinned up in the kitchen. I've talked him down to the executive summary. Thanks for playing it straight.
